newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. State budget 'unlikely' in June - Gov. Pataki.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. State budget 'unlikely' in June - Gov. Pataki.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said Wednesday it is "unlikely" an already late fiscal 1998 state budget will be in place by June.
Pataki, talking to reporters here after a meeting with legislative leaders, said, "I think it's very unlikely that the budget will be in place by June. We're still very much far a part."
While still far apart on some budget issues, Pataki, a Republican, said, "At least there were some signs that there will be some movement, and that we might be able to begin to put things together."
He said of Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, that there was "some greater flexibility and willingness to compromise."

The state budget was due by April 1, the start of the fiscal year. But it has become commonplace for over the last 10 years that the state budget be passed late, a problem usually caused by disagreements along party lines. The state Assembly is dominated Democrats, while Republicans are the majority party in the state Senate.
This year, budget talks are bogged down by a number of issues, with welfare reform proposals and rent regulation dominating the talks. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
